title: Aazmuth flight controller
short_description: Modular, triple-redundant STM32 H7 flight controller with 3 IMUs and 2 barometers on isolated buses.
description: Aazmuth is our flagship flight controller for professional UAVs. It runs on an STM32 H7 (Cortex-M7, up to 480 MHz) and carries 3 IMUs and 2 barometers, each on its own isolated bus, so one noisy or failed sensor does not take down the flight. IMU boards plug in over 20-pin Aazmuth Bus connectors, which means you can swap or upgrade sensors without replacing the controller. Built for defence, industry, agriculture, survey, startups and universities.
features:
Triple IMU and dual barometer redundancy
Isolated sensor buses, so vibration on one does not corrupt the others
Modular IMU boards on the 20-pin Aazmuth Bus
Public pinout, calibration and sensor-integration docs
specifications:
Microcontroller: STM32 H7, Cortex-M7
Clock speed: Up to 480 MHz
Memory: 2 MB flash, 1 MB RAM
Redundancy: 3 IMUs, 2 barometers
Size: 92 x 54 x 14.6 mm
Weight: 63 g
best_for:
Agriculture
Survey and mapping
Defense and security
Education and research
faq:
Q: What redundancy does the Aazmuth flight controller have?
A: Aazmuth carries 3 IMUs and 2 barometers, each on its own isolated bus, so a fault or vibration on one sensor does not corrupt the others.

Q: What processor does Aazmuth use?
A: An STM32 H7 (Cortex-M7) running at up to 480 MHz, with 2 MB of flash and 1 MB of RAM.

Q: How big and heavy is it?
A: 92 x 54 x 14.6 mm and 63 g.

Q: Where are the pinout and calibration guides?
A: In our public documentation. Overview, pinout, calibration, sensor integration and dimensions are all linked on this page.

title: Exelr8 FPV flight controller F7

description: Exelr8 is our F7 flight controller for FPV drones, made for tight, punchy racing and freestyle builds. It pairs with the Skydrive 55A AM32 4-in-1 ESC and the NAVSATE mini GPS to give you a complete Indian-designed FPV stack with local support.

F7 processor

Designed and supported in India
specifications:
Processor: F7
Built for: FPV racing and freestyle
best_for:
FPV racing and freestyle
Startups and prototypes
faq:
Q: What is the Exelr8 flight controller for?
A: Exelr8 is an F7 flight controller for FPV drone builds, including racing and freestyle quads.

Q: Which ESC and GPS go with Exelr8?
A: The Skydrive 55A AM32 4-in-1 ESC and the NAVSATE mini GPS are the matching parts in our FPV stack.

Q: Exelr8 or Aazmuth?
A: Choose Exelr8 for FPV builds and Aazmuth when you need triple-redundant sensing for professional or mission work.

title: Skydrive AM32 60A 3-6S
short_description: 60A AM32 ESC for 3-6S LiPo builds. Handles heavy payloads such as sprayer drones.
description: The Skydrive AM32 60A is a 3-6S electronic speed controller running open AM32 firmware, so you can configure and update it with the usual AM32 tools. Its 60 A rating suits heavy-lift and agriculture drones carrying sprayer payloads.
features:
60 A rating for heavy payloads
AM32 firmware, configurable with standard AM32 tools
3-6S LiPo input
faq:
Q: Which firmware does the Skydrive 60A run?
A: AM32, so you can configure and update it with standard AM32 tools.

Q: What battery does the Skydrive 60A support?
A: 3-6S LiPo.

Q: Is the 60A ESC good for agriculture drones?
A: Yes. The 60 A rating is meant for heavier payloads such as sprayer drones. Tell us your motor and prop setup and we will confirm the fit.

title: Skydrive 55A AM32 4-in-1
short_description: Four 55A AM32 ESCs on one board. Short wiring for 5-inch FPV builds and below.
description: The Skydrive 55A 4-in-1 puts four AM32 ESCs on a single board, which keeps wiring short and the stack tidy on 5-inch FPV builds and smaller. It is the matching ESC for the Exelr8 F7 flight controller.

4 ESCs on one board
55 A rating
AM32 firmware
faq:
Q: What is a 4-in-1 ESC?
A: A single board that carries four speed controllers, one for each motor of a quadcopter, which keeps wiring short and weight low.

Q: Which firmware does the 55A 4-in-1 run?
A: AM32.

Q: What does the NAVSATE GPS do?
A: It tells the flight controller where the drone is and how fast it is moving, which enables position hold, return-to-home and waypoint missions.
